newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 5.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The cabinet is requesting parliament hold a confidence vote during its meeting which begins next Tuesday.
- The cabinet will present parliament with a proposal to establish 13 regions, which it approved yesterday.
- Monopoly natural gas importer, Transgas, is threatened with financial collapse due to the decline of the crown. The Industry and Trade Ministry should intervene and change prices.

- Many economists and experts on housing problems see the attempt of the leader of the Christian Democrats, Josef Lux, to delay deregulation of rents and energy prices as a political maneouvre, for which there is no economic foundation.

- Attractive interest rates for short-term accounts at most banks have caused a wave of deposits of several billion crowns. In the past seven days, Komercni Banka's deposits increased by five percent, which is more than 10 billion crowns.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Less than one week since its first reaction to the exchange rate of the crown and the increase in fuel prices on world markets, Ceska Rafinerska will increase its fuel prices again, this time by an average of 23 hellers per litre.
- The cabinet approved a new law on bankruptcies and settlement yesterday, which should specify conditions for debtors and speed up bankruptcy proceedings.
- Yesterday, the cabinet instructed Transport Minister Martin Riman to make a proposal for financing construction of railway lines in accordance with prepared budget cuts.

- In the middle of April, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus exchanged faxes with the executive director of the IMF, Stanley Fischer, concerning the March report from the IMF warning of possible future developments in the domestic economy. Klaus answered the first fax from April 11 that "Our passivity is not dangerously threatened, since we are completely aware of our current economic situation."

- The disagreement from Czech experts in the Czech-Slovak customs union did not stop the Slovak cabinet's decision on Tuesday introducing a qouta for imports of Czech beer. Bratislava announced yesterday that it is considering the same measures for liqour, cigarettes and margarine.
PRAVO - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus is now in a public conflict with his cabinet and party deputy Josef Zieleniec and other members of his party are also beginning to call for his resignation.

- The chairman of the Czech-Moravian union federation, Richard Falbr, met with President Vaclav Havel on Wednesday to inform him of the unions' opinions of the political and economic situation. Representatives of the cabinet will meet with the federation on Saturday.
- Several physical persons which own nearly 40 percent of Ceska Gumarenska and the food trading concern M-Holding invested both of these shares into a newly established company S.K.I. Trust.
- McDonnell Douglas, which won a tender for Aero Vodochody together with Boeing and CSA, is still trying to begin production of parts for its FA-18 Hornet aircrafts in the Czech Republic.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The Finance Ministry's administration supervising the capital market (UCP) issued fines totalling 2.35 million crowns during May. The UCP revoked the operating licence for the investment company Optimal s.r.o.

- Parliamentary Chairman Milos Zeman announced yesterday in Moscow that the Czech Republic has a good chance to be accepted to NATO during the first wave of expansion. He added that if it was accepted, it would not allow itself to be treated as a second-class member.
- Electrical appliance maker ETA was the favourite brand in the Czech Republic, according to a survey from AISA.
- Technoexport a.s. had revenue last year of 2.2 billion crowns and net profits of 27.8 million crowns. Shareholders, however, will not be paid dividends.
- From today, steel maker Nova Hut will be the 46th company to have its shares listed on the Prague Stock Exchange.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
